correctness.summary: The binary dot-product identity converts cubic acuteness exactly into the hypercube general-position condition. The verifier validates the 24-point input and exhaustively enumerates every deletion set of size 0 through 7, every individually compatible replacement candidate in Q_11, pair compatibility with retained vertices, and all-new triples. No completion with one net extra vertex exists, yielding intersection at most 16 with any 25-point general-position set.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Current sources record the 24-point Q_11 witness and the equivalent cubic-acute, general-position, (2,1)-separating, and binary 2-frameproof formulations, but searches under those formulations plus exchange/local/maximal/overlap terminology found no statement of the 17-point symmetric-difference obstruction or equivalent seven-exchange isolation for this explicit configuration. Existing SCOPE records showed no collision.

value.summary: The result rules out the complete seven-exchange neighborhood around the strongest currently recorded 24-point Q_11 witness. Thus any 25-point improvement must discard at least eight known vertices and introduce at least nine new ones, a concrete structural constraint for future exact or heuristic searches.

limitations: The result is local to one explicit 24-point configuration and its hypercube-automorphic images.
It does not prove gp(Q_11)=24 or exclude structurally distant 25-point sets.
The exhaustive certificate stops at deletion radius seven.
The verification is computational rather than proof-assistant formalized.
Differently indexed frameproof-code literature leaves residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
